title: 34.5 An 18.5-to-23.6GHz Quad-Core Class-F23 Oscillator Without 2nd/3rd Harmonic Tuning Achieving 193dBc/Hz Peak FoM and 140-to-250kHz 1/f3PN Corner in 65nm CMOS
problem: At mm-wave frequencies, coupled quad-core oscillators suffer from Q-factor degradation in small inductors due to destructive coupling, and maintaining optimal phase-noise performance across wide frequency tuning ranges requires complex harmonic alignment—typically requiring supplementary switched-capacitor arrays that further degrade Q-factor.
motivation: Low phase-noise mm-wave oscillators are critical for high-data-rate wireless communications; improving FoM and reducing 1/f³ PN corner enables better jitter performance in PLLs at extreme frequency-division ratios required by 200Gb/s+ transceivers.
method: A quad-core Class-F₂₃ topology coupled in circular configuration using circular-connected transformer-based resonant tanks for high Q-factor with ultra-low inductance. The design achieves automatic harmonic impedance alignment across the full frequency tuning range by eliminating the need for separate 2nd and 3rd harmonic tuning structures, instead relying on the inherent harmonic properties of the F-class topology.
key_novelty: First quad-core Class-F₂₃ oscillator that achieves harmonic alignment without explicit 2nd/3rd harmonic tuning, eliminating tuning-induced Q-factor degradation across a wide 5.1GHz tuning range.
contributions: Circular-connected quad-core topology for improved Q-factor over star-connected designs
Automatic harmonic impedance peak alignment via F-class intrinsic properties, eliminating switched-capacitor arrays
Wide tuning range (18.5–23.6 GHz) with consistent 1/f³ PN corner (140–250 kHz)
Peak FoM of 193 dBc/Hz demonstrating 10 dB FoM improvement over prior work
baselines: circular transformer-based VCO with harmonic tuning
limitations: Specific phase-noise performance metrics at different offsets not provided in abstract.
primary_theme: Low phase-noise quad-core mm-wave oscillator with harmonically-optimized F-class topology
